34609-king-of-the-castle.title: King Of The Castle
34609-king-of-the-castle.creator: George Manville Fenn
34609-king-of-the-castle.description: A book by George Manville Fenn. "Well, there, don't bother me. If you want more money you can have it. You ought to take the lead here, and there were ladies on some of the yachts and on the pier yesterday who quite left you behind.--Yes!

5408-the-rubaiyat-of-omar-khayyam-jr.title: The Rubaiyat Of Omar Khayyam Jr
5408-the-rubaiyat-of-omar-khayyam-jr.creator: Unknown
5408-the-rubaiyat-of-omar-khayyam-jr.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. the quatrains of the first Omar of Naishapur. The genius of the East has, indeed, ever been slow to reveal itself in the West. It took a Crusade to bring to our knowledge anything of the schöner Geist of the Orient; and it was not until the day of Matthew Arnold that the Epic of Persia[1] was brought into the proper realm of English poesy.

arxiv-1611-08983.title: Analyzing the group sparsity based on the rank minimization methods
arxiv-1611-08983.creator: Zhiyuan Zha, Xin Liu, Xiaohua Huang , Henglin Shi , Yingyue Xu , Qiong Wang , Lan Tang , Xinggan Zhang
arxiv-1611-08983.description: Abstract Sparse coding has achieved a great success in various image processing studies. However, there is not any benchmark to measure the sparsity of image patch/group because sparse discriminant conditions cannot keep unchanged. This paper analyzes the sparsity of group based on the strategy of the rank minimization. Firstly, an adaptive dictionary for each group is designed.

arxiv-2004-12404.title: N + 3 {}_{3}^{+} : Full-Dimensional Potential Energy Surface, Vibrational Energy Levels and Ground State Dynamics
arxiv-2004-12404.creator: Debasish Koner, Max Schwilk, Sarbani Patra, Evan J. Bieske, Markus Meuwly
arxiv-2004-12404.description: Abstract The fundamentals and higher vibrationally excited states for the N + 3 {}_{3}^{+} ion in its electronic ground state have been determined from quantum bound state calculations on 3-dimensional potential energy surfaces (PESs) at the CCSD(T)-F12 and MRCI+Q levels of theory.

arxiv-2107-03004.title: Explicit volume formula for a hyperbolic tetrahedron in terms of edge lengths
arxiv-2107-03004.creator: Nikolay Abrosimov, Bao Vuong
arxiv-2107-03004.description: Abstract We consider a compact hyperbolic tetrahedron of a general type. It is a convex hull of four points called vertices in the hyperbolic space ℍ 3 \mathbb{H}^{3} . It can be determined by the set of six edge lengths up to isometry.

arxiv-2201-05425.title: Interpersonal Conflicts During Code Review CCS: Software and its engineering Collaboration in software development CCS: Software and its engineering Software development process management
arxiv-2201-05425.creator: Pavlína Wurzel Gonçalves, Gül Çalıklı, Alberto Bacchelli
arxiv-2201-05425.description: Abstract . Code review consists of manual inspection, discussion, and judgment of source code by developers other than the code’s author. Due to discussions around competing ideas and group decision-making processes, interpersonal conflicts during code reviews are expected. This study systematically investigates how developers perceive code review conflicts and addresses interpersonal conflicts during code reviews as a theoretical construct.

arxiv-2203-12658.title: Computed Tomography Reconstruction Using Generative Energy-Based Priors
arxiv-2203-12658.creator: Martin Zach, Erich Kobler, Thomas Pock
arxiv-2203-12658.description: Abstract In the past decades, Computed Tomography (CT) has established itself as one of the most important imaging techniques in medicine. Today, the applicability of CT is only limited by the deposited radiation dose, reduction of which manifests in noisy or incomplete measurements. Thus, the need for robust reconstruction algorithms arises.

arxiv-2303-17726.title: On difference equations with ‘ B B ’-type solitons on three dimensional lattice.
arxiv-2303-17726.creator: Sergey M. Sergeev
arxiv-2303-17726.description: Abstract In this paper we discuss an example of classical integrable equation with rather unusual ‘B’-type Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) soliton hierarchy. Department of Theoretical Physics, Research School of Physics and Engineering, Australian National University, Canberra, ACT 0200, Australia and Faculty of Science and Technology, University of Canberra, Bruce ACT 2617, Australia 1 Zero curvature problem: the Euler angles.

arxiv-2307-09989.title: UniMatch: A Unified User-Item Matching Framework for the Multi-purpose Merchant Marketing
arxiv-2307-09989.creator: Qifang Zhao, Tianyu Li, Meng Du, Yu Jiang, Qinghui Sun, Zhongyao Wang, Hong Liu, Huan Xu
arxiv-2307-09989.description: Abstract When doing private domain marketing with cloud services, the merchants usually have to purchase different machine learning models for the multiple marketing purposes, leading to a very high cost. We present a unified user-item matching framework to simultaneously conduct item recommendation and user targeting with just one model.

arxiv-2312-05028.title: Cluster images with AntClust: a clustering algorithm based on the chemical recognition system of ants
arxiv-2312-05028.creator: Winfried Gero Oed, and Parisa Memarmoshrefi
arxiv-2312-05028.description: Abstract We implement AntClust , a clustering algorithm based on the chemical recognition system of ants and use it to cluster images of cars. We will give a short recap summary of the main working principles of the algorithm as devised by the original paper [ 1 ] .

arxiv-2410-06024.title: Jet Expansions of Residual Computation
arxiv-2410-06024.creator: Yihong Chen, Xiangxiang Xu, Yao Lu, Pontus Stenetorp, Luca Franceschi
arxiv-2410-06024.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yihong Chen, Xiangxiang Xu, Yao Lu, Pontus Stenetorp, Luca Franceschi. We introduce a framework for expanding residual computational graphs using jets , operators that generalize truncated Taylor series. Our method provides a systematic approach to disentangle contributions of different computational paths to model predictions. In contrast to existing techniques such as distillation, probing, or early decoding, our expansions rely solely on the model itself and requires no data, training, or sampling from the model.

arxiv-2410-21908.title: Cactus scheme, catalecticant minors, and scheme theoretic equations
arxiv-2410-21908.creator: Jarosław Buczyński, Hanieh Keneshlou
arxiv-2410-21908.description: Abstract The r r -th cactus variety of a subvariety X X in a projective space generalizes the r r -th secant variety of X X and it is defined using linear spans of finite subschemes of X X of degree r r . One of its original purposes was to study the vanishing sets of catalecticant minors.

arxiv-2411-10310.title: Assortment Optimization under the Multinomial Logit Model with Covering Constraints
arxiv-2411-10310.description: Abstract We consider an assortment optimization problem under the multinomial logit choice model with general covering constraints. In this problem, the seller offers an assortment that should contain a minimum number of products from multiple categories. We refer to these constraints as covering constraints.

arxiv-2501-10583.title: Inference of response functions with the help of machine learning algorithms
arxiv-2501-10583.creator: Doga Murat Kurkcuoglu, Alessandro Roggero, Gabriel N. Perdue, Rajan Gupta
arxiv-2501-10583.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Doga Murat Kurkcuoglu, Alessandro Roggero, Gabriel N. Perdue, Rajan Gupta. Response functions are a key quantity to describe the near-equilibrium dynamics of strongly-interacting many-body systems. Recent techniques that attempt to overcome the challenges of calculating these ab initio have employed expansions in terms of orthogonal polynomials. We employ a neural network prediction algorithm to reconstruct a response function S ⁡ ( ω ) S(\omega) defined over a range in frequencies ω \omega .

arxiv-2505-12105.title: Flux and Color of WISE 0855-0714
arxiv-2505-12105.creator: Edward Wright, Jack Foley
arxiv-2505-12105.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Edward Wright, Jack Foley. WISE 0855-0714 is the coldest known brown dwarf, located 2.28 pc from the solar system. Discovered by the Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) in 2014 ( Luhman 2014 ) , the object is of interest to scientists because of its low temperature ( ≈ 270 \approx 270 K), proximity to the solar system, small mass ( ∼ 3 − 10 ​ M J \sim 3-10\>M_{J} ), and high proper motion.

arxiv-2506-05201.title: SUSY meets SMEFT: Complete one-loop matching of the general MSSM Preprint: TTK-25-14 P3H-25-036 https://github.com/BSM-EFT/MSSM-to-SMEFT
arxiv-2506-05201.creator: Sabine Kraml, Andre Lessa, Suraj Prakash, and Felix Wilsch
arxiv-2506-05201.description: Abstract We present the complete one-loop matching of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) onto the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), considering the most general case for the MSSM with conserved R R -parity, which has 124 free parameters.

arxiv-2507-08210.title: From Curiosity to Competence: How World Models Interact with the Dynamics of Exploration
arxiv-2507-08210.creator: Fryderyk Mantiuk (fryderyk.mantiuk@student.uni-tuebingen.de), Hanqi Zhou (hanqi.zhou@uni-tuebingen.de), & Charley M. Wu
arxiv-2507-08210.description: Abstract What drives an agent to explore the world while also maintaining control over the environment? From a child at play to scientists in the lab, intelligent agents must balance curiosity (the drive to seek knowledge) with competence (the drive to master and control the environment).

arxiv-2509-00692.title: CascadeFormer: A Family of Two-stage Cascading Transformers for Skeleton-based Human Action Recognition
arxiv-2509-00692.creator: Yusen Peng, Alper Yilmaz
arxiv-2509-00692.description: Abstract Skeleton-based human action recognition leverages sequences of human joint coordinates to identify actions performed in videos. Owing to the intrinsic spatiotemporal structure of skeleton data, Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have been the dominant architecture in this field. However, recent advances in transformer models and masked pretraining frameworks open new avenues for representation learning.

arxiv-2512-19896.title: Gate-Based Microwave Quantum Repeater Via Grid-State Encoding
arxiv-2512-19896.creator: Hany Khalifa, Matti Silveri
arxiv-2512-19896.description: Abstract In autonomous quantum error correction the lifetime of a logical bosonic qubit can be extended beyond its physical constituents without feedback measurements. Leveraging autonomous error correction, we propose a second-generation gate-based microwave quantum repeater (GBMQR) with encoded bosonic grid states.

arxiv-2604-04979.title: Squeez: Task-Conditioned Tool-Output Pruning for Coding Agents
arxiv-2604-04979.creator: Ádám Kovács

plos-pone-0355930.title: Network pharmacology and molecular simulation study on the multi-target gene regulatory mechanism of Isatis indigotica against hepatic inflammation
plos-pone-0355930.creator: XueRu Li, Yang Wang, HuiJun Cheng, Rong Chen, XiaoLu Chen
plos-pone-0355930.description: Network pharmacology and molecular simulation study on the multi-target gene regulatory mechanism of Isatis indigotica against hepatic inflammation

pmc-10574670.title: Is Increasing Diet Diversity of Animal-Source Foods Related to Better Health-Related Quality of Life among Chinese Men and Women?
pmc-10574670.creator: Hui Jing, Yuxin Teng, Samuel Chacha, Ziping Wang, Guoshuai Shi, Baibing Mi, Binyan Zhang, Jiaxin Cai, Yezhou Liu, Qiang Li, Yuan Shen, Jiaomei Yang, Yijun Kang, Shanshan Li, Danmeng Liu, Duolao Wang, Hong Yan, Shaonong Dang, Inmaculada Bautista Castaño
pmc-10574670.description: Diet plays a crucial role in regulating individuals’ lifestyles and is closely related to health. The intake of animal-sourced foods (ASF) provides the human body with high-quality protein and various micronutrients. This study aimed to investigate whether the diversity of animal foods has a positive impact on the health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among residents.

pmc-10638392.title: Bioinspired porous three-coordinated single-atom Fe nanozyme with oxidase-like activity for tumor visual identification via glutathione
pmc-10638392.creator: Da Chen, Zhaoming Xia, Zhixiong Guo, Wangyan Gou, Junlong Zhao, Xuemei Zhou, Xiaohe Tan, Wenbin Li, Shoujie Zhao, Zhimin Tian, Yongquan Qu
pmc-10638392.description: Inspired by structures of natural metalloenzymes, a biomimetic synthetic strategy is developed for scalable synthesis of porous Fe-N3 single atom nanozymes (pFeSAN) using hemoglobin as Fe-source and template. pFeSAN delivers 3.3- and 8791-fold higher oxidase-like activity than Fe-N4 and Fe3O4 nanozymes.

pmc-11511120.title: Presence of Ochratoxin A Residues in Blood Serum of Slaughtered Pigs in Greece
pmc-11511120.creator: Mikela Vlachou, Andreana Pexara, Nikolaos Solomakos, Alexander Govaris, Dimitrios Palaiogiannis, Vassilis Athanasiadis, Stavros I Lalas
pmc-11511120.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study aimed to assess the presence of ochratoxin A (OTA) residues in the blood serum of slaughtered pigs in Greece. Samples were obtained from 1695 healthy slaughtered pigs originating from 113 different farms located in 21 geographic regional units in 8 different geographic regions of Greece and were analyzed using an immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and high-performance liquid chromatography with fluorescence detector (HPLC-FD).

pmc-11604761.title: Million-Q free space meta-optical resonator at near-visible wavelengths
pmc-11604761.creator: Jie Fang, Rui Chen, David Sharp, Enrico M. Renzi, Arnab Manna, Abhinav Kala, Sander A. Mann, Kan Yao, Christopher Munley, Hannah Rarick, Andrew Tang, Sinabu Pumulo, Yuebing Zheng, Vinod M. Menon, Andrea Alù, Arka Majumdar
pmc-11604761.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). High-quality (Q)-factor optical resonators with extreme temporal coherence are of both technological and fundamental importance in optical metrology, continuous-wave lasing, and semiconductor quantum optics. Despite extensive efforts in designing high-Q resonators across different spectral regimes, the experimental realization of very large Q-factors at visible wavelengths remains challenging due to the small feature size that is sensitive to fabrication imperfections, and thus is typically implemented in integrated photonics.

pmc-11606837.title: Neuroprotective Roles of Lauric Acid and Resveratrol: Shared Benefits in Neuroinflammation and Anxiety, Distinct Effects on Memory Enhancement
pmc-11606837.creator: Betul Kisioglu, Esra Onal, Derya Karabulut, Ilyas Onbasilar, Asli Akyol
pmc-11606837.description: Neuroinflammation can be triggered by a high‐fat/high‐fructose diet (HFFD), and CD36 may be an underlying mechanism. Lauric acid (LA), the major fatty acid in coconut oil, and resveratrol, the plant‐based polyphenolic compound, may exert anti‐inflammatory effects. Therefore, this study investigated the possible effects of LA and resveratrol on diet‐induced neuroinflammation and CD36.

pmc-12470352.title: Bronchoscopy in the Pediatric Cardiovascular Patient with Persistent Respiratory Pathology
pmc-12470352.creator: Ana-Belen Ariza-Jimenez, Delia Valverde Montoro, Pilar Caro Aguilera, Estela Perez Ruiz, Francisco Javier Perez Frias, Warwick Butt
pmc-12470352.description: Background: Patients with congenital heart disease can associate malformations. The most frequent complications are those related to the airways, which produce prolonged cardiovascular postoperative. Objectives: Describe pathology, bronchoscopy indications, and findings in patients with heart pathology and persistent breath failure to improve prognosis and determine an early treatment.

pmc-12618785.title: Metabolomics and metabolites in cancer diagnosis and treatment
pmc-12618785.creator: Minyi Cai, Haiyan Liu, Chen Shao, Tingting Li, Jun Jin, Yahui Liang, Jinhu Wang, Ji Cao, Bo Yang, Qiaojun He, Xuejing Shao, Meidan Ying
pmc-12618785.description: Cancer is a leading cause of death worldwide. Metabolic reprogramming in cancers plays an important role in tumor initiation, malignant progression and therapeutic response. Based on this, significant progress has been made in the development of the metabolite-based early cancer detection and targeted interventions.

pmc-12713299.title: Climate change is leading to geographic expansion of tropical birds—range expansion and niche modeling in the White-browed Crake (Pololimnas cinereus)
pmc-12713299.creator: Zhao Wanglin, Suo Lang, Wang Ting, Wang Yuan, Fan Liqing, Luo Tianxiang, Wang Xingxing, Yang Le, Zhang Lin
pmc-12713299.description: BackgroundThe White-browed Crake (Pololimnas cinereus, family: Rallidae, hereafter WbC) is a climate sensitive bird with a tropical/subtropical distribution in Southeast Asia, Australasia, and the Philippines. Range expansion into higher latitudes would be predicted for this species in a warming climate. In this study, we first photographed a WbC in a park of Motuo County on the southeast Tibetan Plateau.

pmc-12730151.title: Updates on the Role of Innate Immunity’s Pattern Recognition Receptors in Vitiligo Pathogenesis and Therapeutic Potential
pmc-12730151.creator: Jindi Feng, Lu Lu, Huimin He, Yubin Peng, Shiyu Zhang, Lu Yang, Yuehua Liu, Tao Wang
pmc-12730151.description: Vitiligo is a complex, multifactorial disorder characterized by acquired skin pigment loss that strongly influences the physical and mental well-being of patients with vitiligo. The precise pathogenesis remains incompletely elucidated, but recent studies emphasize the significant roles of both innate and adaptive immunity. Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs), essential for innate immune sensing, significantly contribute to melanocyte destruction in vitiligo.

pmc-12985801.title: Envisioning the Heart
pmc-12985801.creator: Philip Alexander, Muhammad Umair
pmc-12985801.description: Philip Alexander, MD, is a native Texan, retired physician, and accomplished musician and artist. After 41 years as an internal medicine physician, Dr. Phil retired from his practice in College Station in 2016. A lifelong musician and former music professor, he often performs as an oboe soloist for the Brazos Valley Symphony Orchestra.

pmc-13003045.title: The emerging role of TLR7-mediated signaling in respiratory viral infections and autoimmune diseases
pmc-13003045.creator: Chenxiao Wang, Jefferson F Evangelista, Ana Karina Nisperuza Vidal, Mohammad Islamuddin, Yilin Chen, Donghua Xu, Xuebin Qin
pmc-13003045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Toll-like receptor 7 (TLR7) is a key endosomal sensor that detects single-stranded RNA, linking innate and adaptive immunity through the induction of type I interferons and proinflammatory cytokines. Recent studies have underscored the pivotal role of TLR7 in shaping immune responses to respiratory viral infections, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), as well as in the pathogenesis of systemic autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which can be triggered by the respiratory viral infections.

pmc-13213536.title: DOES AEROBIC EXERCISE AFFECT MEMORY, ATTENTION, WORKING MEMORY, AND FATIGUE AFTER ACQUIRED BRAIN INJURY? A SINGLE-BLINDED, RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED PILOT STUDY
pmc-13213536.creator: Eygló INGÓLFSDÓTTIR, Ulla BERGFELDT, Märta Berthold LINDSTEDT, Lennart BERGFELDT, Tie-Qiang LI, Tomas JONSSON, Marika C. MÖLLER
pmc-13213536.description: ObjectiveTo explore potential effects of aerobic exercise on cognitive function, fatigue, and neuroplasticity after stroke or traumatic brain injury.DesignA randomized controlled pilot study.Subjects/PatientsTwelve participants, 10 men and 2 women aged 16–65 years diagnosed with acquired brain injury (moderate to severe stroke or traumatic brain injury), enrolled in an outpatient rehabilitation programme at least 3 months post-injury.

pmc-13440031.title: Mepce Restrains Ferroptosis in Prostate Cancer Through 7SK–P‐TEFb Pause Control
pmc-13440031.creator: Tongtong Zhang, Xiangyang Zhan, Jiexiang Zhang, Mingyue Tan, Chuanmin Chu, Guanqun Ju, Xinyu Zhai, Jianyi Gu, Huirong Zhu, Dongliang Xu
pmc-13440031.description: Ferroptosis can be therapeutically induced through GPX4 inhibition, but the mechanisms that determine ferroptosis sensitivity in prostate cancer remain incompletely understood. Here, we combined genome‐wide CRISPR screening under graded GPX4 inhibition with mechanistic perturbation–rescue experiments and validation in xenograft and immunocompetent syngeneic prostate cancer models. We identified MEPCE loss as a conserved sensitizer to ferroptosis.

pmc-13500735.title: Analysis of adverse pregnancy outcomes among pregnant women in Hunan Province from 2015 to 2023: Incidence, temporal trends, and risk factors
pmc-13500735.creator: Jiezhi MA, Wenxiu CHEN, Lingyi LIU, Shuijing YI, Pu TIAN
pmc-13500735.description: ObjectiveIn recent years, China has witnessed marked changes in the fertility environment and the composition of women of childbearing age, making the prevention and control of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) a major challenge for maternal and infant health management. This study aims to investigate the incidence, trends, and risk factors for APOs in Hunan Province from 2015 to 2023.
